div.head: Grið 21.2
div.ab: We witan, þæt þurh Godes gyfe þræl wearð to ðegene ⁊ ceorl wearð to eorle, sangere to sacerde ⁊ bocere to biscpe.
We witan þæt, þurh Godes gyfe, þræl wearð to ðegene and ceorl wearð to eorle, sangere to sacerde and bocere to biscpe.
Wir wissen, dass durch Gottes Gnade ein Knecht zum Vornehmen wurde und ein Gemeiner zum Adligen [Grafen?] wurde, ein Sänger zum Priester und ein Schreiber zum Bischof.
We know that through God's grace a slave became a thegn and a ceorl became a nobleman [earl?], a singer [became] a priest and a scribe a bishop.
We know that, through God’s grace, a slave has become a thane and a commoner become a nobleman, a choir singer become a priest, and a scholar become a bishop.
div.note: The pairs are alliterating, Liebermann notes.

note.seg: Mitte 11. Jhs. beweist das Nord. Lehnwort þræl, schon seit Atr allgemein aufgenommen, nicht etwa Nordenglischen Abfassungsort; vgl. Pogatscher in Gött. Gel. Anz. 1894, 1015. Vgl. Gl Stand 10. Wulfstan 162f. beklagt als Ergebnis der schweren Dänennot die soziale Ständeverschiebung: oft þræt þæne þegen, þe ær wæs his hlaford, wyrcð to þræle

In the mid-11th cent. the Norse loanword þræl, generally adopted ever since Atr, does not, say, prove a Northern English place of composition; cf. Pogatscher in Gött. Gel. Anz. 1894, 1015. Cf. Gl Stand 10. Wulfstan 162f. laments the social shifting of ranks as the result of the grievous Danish distress: oft þræt þæne þegen, þe ær wæs his hlaford, wyrcð to þræle

Zwar pflegt eorl neben ceorl in der Reimformel die alte Bed. ‘vornehm’ sonst zu behalten. Hier aber wollte vielleicht Verf. (wie in vor. Z. den Gemeinfreien) absichtlich die Zwischenstufe des Thegn überspringen und meinte ‘Grafen’

It is true that eorl beside ceorl in the rhyming formula usually keeps the old meaning ‘noble’ elsewhere. Here, however, the author perhaps deliberately meant to pass over the intermediate rank of the thegn (as with the common freeman in the preceding l.) and meant ‘earls’
Vgl. Geþyncðo 7; Gl Geistliche 9a. Die Alliteration biscopas ⁊ boceras hat auch das Epos Andreas 607. Sume boceras—also Anfänger in der Bildung—weorðað wisfæste; Dichtung Manna wyrd. 71
Cf. Geþyncðo 7; Gl Geistliche 9a. The alliteration biscopas ⁊ boceras also occurs in the epic Andreas 607. Sume boceras—hence beginners in learning—weorðað wisfæste; the poem Manna wyrd. 71
